name: US jobless claims
summary: US jobless claims 4-week average 195k, at its 52-week low
state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, keeping the four-week average at about 194,750, its 52-week low and far from the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED). Layoffs remained low as of 6 Nov.
for_you: A tight labour market supports household incomes; a sustained rise in claims would be the first sign of job losses spreading.
rubric_hit: 4-week average 0% above its 52-week low, below the 15% Watch line
why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
